svg.title: keyguard: a commit blocked, and blocked again with --no-verify
svg.desc: A terminal. The command git commit prints keyguard: commit blocked: 1 finding, with a table of file, line, type, secret and why. The secret column shows only the shape sk_live_…a1B2. The same commit with --no-verify prints keyguard: ref update blocked: 1 finding, because the key is one keyguard learned; that table starts with a commit column. git then stops with a fatal line. Beside each block, outside the terminal, a tag names the layer that stopped it and the verdict BLOCKED. A thin crawler, a net of small glowing dots on hairlines, sits in the right margin and reaches out to both tags and to the key on the diff above them.

g.text: fix: move the value to a gitignored .env and read it from the environment.
do not bypass with --no-verify: real keys are also blocked at the
ref level, and GitHub is re-scanned every minute.
COMMIT FILE LINE TYPE SECRET WHY
fix: move the value to a gitignored .env and read it from the environment.
do not bypass with --no-verify: real keys are also blocked at the
ref level, and GitHub is re-scanned every minute.
fatal: in 'prepared' phase, update aborted by the reference-transaction hook
